title: Narrow the governance reading rule and retry a refused reading once
summary: Reading acceptance stops requiring a governance path for bare common words (deploy, config, ci, gate…); it requires one only when the request names the governance path or a file under it, or a deliverable implies it (GOVERNANCE_BY_DELIVERABLE stays). When any reading rule refuses a reading, the reader is run once more at once with the refusal text as a correction, only a second refusal fails, and the reader brief lists each reading rule in one line. Audience: the drain operator and the reader agent.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for the narrowed rule and the retry; fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test criteria.
Criteria run tests showing acceptance, refusal and the refusal text reaching the second read.
Fixes both the over-broad keyword rule and the missing refusal feedback to the reader.
One change across the named files only.
The retry and rule list are enforced in code and tests.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy, fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The in-run retry belongs in Athena::read_for (reading.rs), which every read path calls, so first reads, rereads after correction and config rereads all get it; drain.rs changes only as far as its failure counting or tests need.

The refusal text is passed to the reader through a new ReaderInputs field rendered as a correction section in reader_brief (briefs.rs); no prompt file under the token budget changes, since the reader prompt set has only 3 tokens left.
Rule list in the brief is one short line per rule: prior result and change scope, criteria evidence, governance coverage, and the reading-build validity checks.

The keyword table is replaced by path-naming detection: the request text contains the governance path (e.g. athena.toml, defaults.toml, setup.sh, rust-toolchain.toml) or a path under .github/workflows/.
Both invocations of the reader are recorded, or at minimum the second reading and its cost are, so budget accounting stays correct.

acceptance_criteria.text: A unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs shows a request that only mentions words from the old keyword table (e.g. 'deploy', 'config', 'ci', 'gate') with no governance path named is accepted by check_governance_coverage; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

A unit test shows a request naming a governance path (e.g. athena.toml or .github/workflows/ci.yml) whose reading leaves it uncovered is still refused, and is accepted once it is listed and named in a criterion or named in out_of_scope; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

A test with a fake reader whose first reading is refused shows the refusal text appears in the second read's brief and the second reading is accepted and recorded; a second refusal is reported as a failure. Run `cargo test`.
reader_brief names each reading rule in one line and the existing brief size test passes; run `cargo test -p athena-context`.
GOVERNANCE_BY_DELIVERABLE is unchanged and a deliverable that is a governance file with no criterion naming it is still refused.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the narrowed governance rule and the one-time re-read with the refusal text.

out_of_scope: athena.toml, defaults.toml and other governance files
Prompt files under the token budget (frame.reader, contract)
departures: Cost and time are higher than the reference: the change spans the reading flow, the brief, and tests with a fake reader, and requires a cold full test and clippy run.
urgent_reason: It cuts failed drains and repeated refused readings (three drains stopped, three refusals of its own fix) by retrying once with the refusal text.
hard_reason: It changes the reading-acceptance gate that judges every other job's reading and the retry path that decides whether a drain item fails.
